sections.title: Overview of Dock Appointment Scheduling
sections.text:
5.1 Overview of Dock Appointment Scheduling
The process of dock scheduling is a valuable tool for businesses looking to
optimize their use of resources and improve efficiency in their supply chain
operations. By reducing wait times for truck drivers during the loading and
unloading of goods, your business can minimize overcrowding and congestion,
particularly on traditionally busy days like Mondays and Fridays. A delay in the
dock scheduling process can lead to increased detention charges and negatively
impact the operational margins of a warehouse. On the other hand, an accurate
dock scheduling system can revolutionize warehouse dock operations and
drastically improve traffic flow, leading to more efficient and cost-effective
supply chain management During loading and unloading operations at docks,
delays can occur, which can put pressure on warehouse operators to work
quickly to meet manufacturing or distribution schedules. This rush can increase
the risk of safety incidents occurring.
© 

321
By scheduling appointments in advance, warehouses can effectively plan and
manage their staff for receiving and shipping processes, as well as allocate their
equipment resources efficiently. This feature helps minimize delays and idle
time for trucks waiting to be loaded or unloaded. Providing carriers with a link to
your warehouse’s dock appointment system can reduce the need for phone-
based or email bookings, resulting in shorter wait times and faster responses for
carriers.
Dock appointment scheduling systems are often integrated into warehouse or
transportation management software, offering a range of helpful features. These
features may include online booking portals, automated appointment
confirmations, and real-time visibility into dock availability and traffic
conditions. These capabilities allow for smoother, more streamlined operations,
reducing wait times and improving overall efficiency in the supply chain.
Efficient planning of vehicle arrivals and departures for unloading and loading
goods is crucial to ensure a well-organized running of the warehouse and to
balance the workload throughout the working day.
Scheduling dock appointments in advance can help prevent appointment
blowouts during the week and reduce the traffic on busy days at the warehouse.
The ultimate goal is to ensure the efficient use of warehouse doors, parking
spaces, and yard checkpoints for loading and unloading trucks from various
carriers while avoiding interruptions in warehouse operations. Allowing carriers
to schedule their own appointments online helps them plan their routes
effectively and eliminates the need to arrive early to ensure they can pick up or
deliver in a timely manner.
The efficient scheduling of dock appointments can be instrumental in
optimizing staffing levels and averting scenarios of understaffing or overstaffing.
This optimization, in turn, can result in enhanced labor planning, a pivotal
component of warehouse operations. A dock scheduling system serves as a
valuable tool for capacity and resource planning, allowing for seamless
communication between carriers and the system, while simultaneously
providing real-time visibility to customers, warehouse personnel, suppliers, and
carriers. By means of dock appointment scheduling, carriers and warehouse
users can coordinate appointments for incoming vehicles or transportation units
(TUs) during loading and unloading processes.
The scheduling process can be executed online, meaning vendors and carriers
can book appointments and track progress in real-time using software.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

322
Additionally, dock appointment scheduling software can be seamlessly
integrated with warehouse management systems (WMS) or transportation
management systems. Streamlined dock appointment scheduling can result in
optimized hours of service, enhanced warehouse efficiency, improved partner
collaboration, and augmented inventory turns. A dock scheduling system may
also include reporting functionalities, such as audits on delivered loads, which
can facilitate the automatic recording and transmission of compliance
information.
SAP provides a web browser-based application called SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling. This application enables efficient planning of vehicle arrivals in
warehouses and allows carriers to enroll their TUs for the yard, book time slots
for loading and unloading, and view the workload at each loading point for each
day.
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling can be deployed as a standalone solution or
integrated with a local SAP EWM system. To use SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling functionalities, SAP has provided the standard Transaction NWBC or
several SAP Fiori applications, as shown in Figure 5.1.
Additionally, an SAP Fiori app called the Dock Appointment Scheduling for
Carriers app is available in SAP S/4HANA to offer a user interface (UI) for carriers.
When integrating SAP EWM and SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling, the
scheduling appointment serves as the planning object for the transport.
Planning is performed using time slots for loading points and defined capacities,
with carriers collaborating via web access. In extended warehouse management
(EWM), the TU is the processing object for the transport.
Figure 5.1 SAP Fiori Apps for SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
The integration of SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling with a local SAP EWM
system allows for the linkage of loading appointments with TU or vehicle
© 

323
activities in SAP EWM. This integration facilitates the exchange of loading
appointment status updates and related TU activity information between SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling and SAP EWM. Additionally, the shipping cockpit
in SAP EWM can be used to track outbound loading appointments created in SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling. Overall, the integration of SAP EWM and SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling provides several benefits for both inbound and
outbound processes.
The requirements for integrating SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the
following:
1. You have enabled the business function SCM_EWM_FND (EWM, Essential
Foundation Functions).
2. You have configured the Basis customization setting for SAP EWM.
3. Within SAP EWM, you have established configurations for means of
transport. Additionally, you have created a connection between packaging
materials and TUs via the SAP Easy Access menu transaction.
4. Within SAP EWM, you have defined a number range for the TU. Note that the
number range for TU numbers must not be the same as the number range
for the loading appointment numbers.
5. You have defined a number range for vehicles in SAP EWM, if applicable.
6. You have defined a number range for shipping and receiving activities in
SAP EWM.
7. You have defined a number range for appointment numbers under the
customization path in SAP EWM.
Some crucial concepts utilized in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the
following:
Docking locations
A docking location refers to a collection of loading points, such as a
warehouse or distribution center, and represents the physical location of
these loading points. This element allows for the definition of attributes that
are uniform across the entire location, such as an address.
If you’re using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling in conjunction with SAP
EWM, a docking location represents an SAP EWM warehouse in SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling. You can specify if the loading points are integrated
with SAP EWM within the docking location. Imperative is that the integration
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

324
with SAP EWM be consistent for all the loading points in a docking location, as
well as the docking location itself. Docking locations can be established by a
user with role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR.
Loading points
Loading appointments for vehicles are organized based on loading points. A
loading point represents a group of warehouse docks that share the same
processing characteristics, such as loading or unloading. In practice, these
“docks” could be fuel dispensers, loading docks, or any location where goods
are received or dispatched from a warehouse. You can combine the loading
points of a particular geographical location into a docking location.
When using docking locations, a crucial requirement is that the integration
with SAP EWM is consistent for all the loading points belonging to a docking
location as well as for the docking location itself. However, if docking
locations are not used, you can specify whether a loading point is integrated
with SAP EWM for each loading point individually.
Loading appointments are scheduled at the loading point level, which is a
collection of warehouse docks with similar attributes. Each loading point is
allocated a defined time slot duration and a range of appointment numbers.
Loading points can be established by a user with the role
/SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR.
Time slots
To plan the times for loading appointments, time slots are used. The duration
of each time slot is defined within the loading point and is fixed across all
time slots. When creating loading points and assigning them to a docking
location, the time slot duration can be specified in the docking location. The
system will automatically use this duration for new loading points.
When modifying a time slot duration is necessary, such as when using a
greater number of time slots with shorter durations to enhance planning, you
can change this duration individually in each loading point. This modification
has no impact on previously generated time slots and their loading
appointments and only applies to new time slots generated for upcoming
time frames. A user with the role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR can create
time slots.
Time slot management
This function allows you to create time slots for a loading point and adjust its
capacity. The fixed duration of each time slot is defined in the loading point’s
© 

325
master data. Each time slot has a capacity, which indicates the maximum
number of vehicles that can be loaded or unloaded simultaneously during
that time slot.
To create time slots, you would define the working time of the loading point
by specifying the start date of the first time slot and specify the capacity for
each time slot according to the circumstances at that time. In this way, you
can adjust the capacity for each time slot by taking into account factors such
as staff availability.
If you’re using the graphical view, you can set the capacity for time slots for
one day and then copy these values forward to the next day. Once you’ve
created the time slot capacity for the week, you can carry these values
forward for the next several weeks. The system automatically sets the
capacity to 0 for days when the loading point is not available, such as public
holidays, based on the factory calendar assigned to the loading point.
You can also change the capacity of time slots for a loading point or delete all
future time slots for a loading appointment after a certain date. If you need to
delete time slots in the future that already have loading appointments
associated with them, you must cancel the loading appointments. If you want
to delete a loading point, you must delete all the time slots and appointments
associated with it.
Appointment management
This function enables you to create and edit loading appointments for loading
points. You can use loading appointments to plan vehicle arrivals at your
warehouse and to balance the workload across the working day.
You can assign more than one time slot to a loading appointment. In this way,
you can plan flexibly for loading appointments that require different amounts
of time for loading or unloading. For example, in a loading point with a time
slot duration of 15 minutes, you can create one loading appointment that
lasts for 30 minutes, perhaps to unload a small delivery, and then create
another loading appointment that lasts for 90 minutes, perhaps to unload a
larger delivery with more handling units (HUs).
Appointments of variable duration
You can create loading appointments of different durations by assigning more
than one time slot to a loading appointment. The shortest
loading appointment possible is one time slot. The longest
loading appointment possible is 7 days. Each loading appointment must
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

326
consist of consecutive time slots. If you need to create a
loading appointment that includes some time when no workers are available
at the loading point, you must include this time in the duration of
the appointment.
Provisional appointments
When working with docking locations, you can create loading appointments
for a docking location without specifying a loading appointment, without
specifying time slots, or both. These loading appointments have the status
Provisional. Provisional appointments do not fill any capacity in a loading
point, and you cannot process provisional appointments without further
planning. When you enter a loading point and time slots into a provisional
appointment, the loading appointment status changes to Planned, and it fills
capacity at the loading point. You can then proceed with the
loading appointment.
Managing loading appointments
You can change loading appointments, when the expected vehicle has not yet
arrived at its checkpoint, to different time slots in the loading point. However,
appointment planners for carriers can change the time slots of their
loading appointments only if the restricted planning period has not begun.
As long as both loading points are in the same docking location, you can
change a loading appointment to a different loading point if the vehicle has
not yet arrived at the warehouse. If you’re using docking locations, the new
loading point must have the same docking location as the original loading
point. You can cancel loading appointments if the vehicle has not yet arrived
at the checkpoint.
Indicating loading appointment direction
You can specify whether a loading appointment is an
inbound appointment or an outbound appointment, if required.
Creating loading appointments for time slots without free capacity
You can create loading appointments for a time slot at your loading point
even if there is no free capacity for the slot. However, appointment planners
for carriers can create loading appointments for time slots with free capacity
only.
Indicating that a loading appointment has arrived at the dock
If you’re using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling without integration
with SAP EWM, you can indicate that a vehicle has arrived at the dock without
© 

327
first indicating that the vehicle has arrived at the checkpoint. You can also
indicate that a vehicle has departed from the checkpoint without first
indicating that the vehicle has departed from the dock.
Changing the date and time after the action is performed
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling saves a record of the time when you
update the status of each loading appointment. You can change the date and
time related to actions for the loading appointment after the actions are
performed. For example, if you set the status of a
loading appointment to Departed from Checkpoint later than when the
vehicle actually left, you can enter the actual time of departure in
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. You can then store these actual times for
later analysis. Appointments can be created by a user with the role
DAS_EXT_CARR_PLANNER.
Table 5.1 provides further information on the various roles involved in SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling.
Role Role Description
/SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR Administrator for Dock Appointment
Scheduling
/SCWM/DAS_SPECIALIST Specialist for Dock Appointment
Scheduling
/SCWM/DAS_CP_CLERK Checkpoint Clerk for Dock Appointment
Scheduling
/SCWM/DAS_EXT_CARR_PLANNER Appointment Planner for Carrier in Dock
Appointment Scheduling
/SCWM/EWM_TO_DAS_INTEGRATION Technical Role for EWM Integration to
Dock Appointment Scheduling
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

328
Role Role Description
/SCWM/DAS_TO_EWM_INTEGRATION Technical Role for Dock Appointment
Scheduling Integration to EWM
Table 5.1 Role Matrix
Your options for SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the following:
Appointment TU (planning in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling)
As shown in Figure 5.2, in this option, an appointment is generated in SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling, which triggers the automatic creation of a TU
in SAP EWM.
Figure 5.2 Appointment Creates TU
TU creates appointment (planning in SAP EWM)
As shown in Figure 5.3, TU is generated in SAP EWM, which triggers loading
appointments in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling.
Figure 5.3 TU Generated in SAP EWM
© 

329

sections.title: Dock Appointment Planning
sections.text:
5.2 Dock Appointment Planning
This section delves into a few scenarios with dock appointment planning: one
scenario where the TU is created without yard management (which we’ll focus
on in Section 5.2.1) and another scenario using yard management, where the TU
is created in SAP EWM first (which we’ll cover in Section 5.2.2).

sections.title: Inbound Process in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
sections.text:
5.2.1 Inbound Process in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
Let’s take a deeper look into the inbound goods receipt business process,
specifically the scenario where a TU is created without yard management, based
on dock appointment planning.
In this business process, the dock appointment serves as a planning object and
is first planned in the SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling module. The next step
is the creation of a TU in SAP EWM.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 5.4, the business process for dock appointment planning
without yard management involves the following steps:
After receiving information about a delivery and its scheduled date, the
carrier’s appointment planner logs on to SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling. Via the web-based application, this user creates an
appointment for the delivery date.
The appointment planner enters the warehouse’s docking location and
the purchase order as a reference document. The system automatically
calculates the loading point, appointment duration, and the number of
required time slots based on the purchase order data. The carrier then
selects a suitable start time slot.
At least 1 day prior to the delivery date, the warehouse clerk reviews the
scheduled appointments for the next day. This user ensures that enough
capacity at the loading point is available to accommodate the planned
1
2
3
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

330
trucks for unloading. If necessary, the warehouse clerk reschedules the
appointment or increases the available workforce in the warehouse.
Upon the truck’s arrival, the driver provides the appointment number to
the checkpoint clerk. The checkpoint clerk then searches for the
appointment in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling using the
appointment number and changes the status to Arrived at Checkpoint.
Subsequently, the checkpoint clerk finds an available door in SAP EWM,
creates a planned door activity, and guides the truck to the designated
door. The truck driver takes the delivery note to the goods receipt
department, where a goods receipt office clerk locates the corresponding
inbound delivery in SAP EWM.
A warehouse worker confirms the truck’s arrival at the door and begins
unloading the truck. A warehouse clerk cross-checks the goods with the
delivery note and brings the revised delivery note to the goods receipt
office. The goods receipt office clerk records the goods receipt, and the
system automatically generates and prints warehouse orders for the
inbound delivery. These warehouse orders facilitate the movement of
goods into the warehouse. Subsequently, the truck leaves the door, and
a warehouse clerk updates the status to Departed from Door.
Figure 5.4 Dock Appointment Planning Creates TU without Yard Management
The truck proceeds to the checkpoint, and the checkpoint clerk searches
for the appointment in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling using the
4
5
6
© 

331
appointment number and then updates the status to Departed from
Checkpoint. The warehouse worker transfers the goods from the goods
receipt area to their respective storage types within the warehouse.
Towards the end of the week or the month, the warehouse clerk selects
all the appointments from the previous week or month in the Analyze
Appointments screen to analyze the waiting and processing times as
well as the disparities between planned and actual times. The warehouse
clerk determines the number of trucks that arrived on time and whether
the processing time aligns with the planned times.
Configuration
In this section, we’ll cover the key customization steps required for this process,
assuming that the main SAP EWM customization settings have already been
configured in the system:
1. Configure a docking location
This configuration setting is required for the creation of a docking location
in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Users with an administrator role can
follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Dock Appointment Scheduling •
Settings • Simple Setup • Simple Setup of Integrated Dock Appointment
Scheduling • Create/Maintain Docking Location or use Transaction NWBC.
To configure a docking location, input the warehouse number, click
Continue, and maintain the Docking Location field, as shown in Figure 5.5.
Figure 5.5 Configuring a Docking Location
2. Configure a loading point
This configuration setting is needed to create loading points in SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling. Users with an administrator role can follow the
7
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

332
SAP NetWeaver menu path Dock Appointment Scheduling • Settings •
Simple Setup • Simple Setup of Integrated Dock Appointment
Scheduling • Create/Maintain Loading Point. Maintain the Loading Point
and Docking Location fields as well as any other details required by your
business processes, as shown in Figure 5.6.
Figure 5.6 Configuring a Loading Point
3. Configure the determination of loading points
This configuration setting is needed to configure how loading points are
determined in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Users with an
administrator role can follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Dock
Appointment Scheduling • Settings • Simple Setup • Simple Setup of
Integrated Dock Appointment Scheduling • Determine Loading Point or
execute Transaction /SCWM/DSDETLP in SAP EWM. Click New Entries and
maintain the Loading Point and Docking Location fields, as shown in
Figure 5.7.
Figure 5.7 Configuring Determination of Loading Point
4. Configure the determination of appointment duration
This configuration setting is needed to configure how appointment duration
is determined in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Users with an
administrator role can follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Dock
Appointment Scheduling • Settings • Simple Setup • Configure
Appointment Duration Determination or execute Transaction
/SCWM/DSCONFDUR in SAP EWM. Click New Entries and fill out the fields in
© 

333
the Configure Appointment Duration Determination section, as shown in
Figure 5.8.
Figure 5.8 Configuring Determination of Appointment Duration
5. Configure integration to other systems
This configuration setting is needed for the integration settings of loading
appointments when SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling is integrated to
other systems, for example, SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. This configuration
defines the SAP ERP system of the purchase order referenced in the loading
appointment. Users with an administrator role can follow the SAP
NetWeaver menu path Dock Appointment Scheduling • Settings • Simple
Setup • Interfaces • Interface Settings for Dock Appointment Scheduling
or execute Transaction /SCWM/DSINT in SAP EWM. Click New Entries and
assign docking locations by maintaining the Docking Location and
Business System for ERP fields and then select all three checkboxes, as
shown in Figure 5.9.
Figure 5.9 Configuring Integration to Other System
6. Configure assignment of door to a loading point
This configuration setting is enables the assignment of doors to a loading
point. Users with an administrator role can follow the SAP NetWeaver menu
path Dock Appointment Scheduling Menu • Settings • Simple Setup •
Simple Setup of Integrated Dock Appointment Scheduling • Assign
Doors to Loading Points or execute Transaction NWBC. Then, maintain the
Loading Point and Warehouse Number fields, as shown in Figure 5.10.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

334
Figure 5.10 Configuring Assignment of Door to a Loading Point
7. Configure time slots for the loading point
This configuration setting defines the time slots of a loading point. Users
with an administrator role can follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Dock
Appointment Scheduling • Settings • Simple Setup • Simple Setup of
Integrated Dock Appointment Scheduling • Create Time Slots in
Graphical View or execute Transaction NWBC, maintain the Loading Point,
Start Date, and Time fields. Click Continue and create time slots as
needed, as shown in Figure 5.11.
Figure 5.11 Configuring Time Slots of a Loading Point
8. Configure an appointment planner for a carrier
This configuration setting is needed to enable carrier appointment
planners, who are external users, to book appointments directly in SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling. Using external web access, users with an
administrator role can follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Dock
Appointment Scheduling • Settings • Simple Setup • Simple Setup of
Integrated Dock Appointment Scheduling • Create Appointment
Planners for Carrier or execute Transaction NWBC. Maintain the Carrier
Number field and press (Enter). Then, configure individual appointment
planners for the carrier by maintaining the Appointment… and User
columns, and then click Save, as shown in Figure 5.12.
© 

335
Figure 5.12 Configuring an Appointment Planner for Carrier
9. Define control parameters for forming vehicles and Tus
You can control how vehicles and TUs are formed in the system. In this
configuration setting, the link between packaging material (of a TU) and
means of transport will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM
Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management
• Cross-Process setting • Shipping and Receiving • General Setting •
Define Control Parameter for Forming Vehicles/Transportation Unit.
Click New Entries and maintain the Means of Trans. field, as shown in
Figure 5.13.
Figure 5.13 Define Control Parameters for Forming Vehicles and TUs
10. Define a product group type
In this configuration setting, a product group type will be defined. This
product group type is assigned to product groups. Follow the IMG menu
path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • SCM Basis • Master Data •
Product • Product Group • Define Product Group Type. Click New Entries
and maintain product group types via the ProdGrType and Description
columns, as shown in Figure 5.14.
Figure 5.14 Define Product Group Type
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

336
11. Define a product group
In this configuration setting, a product group will be defined. A product
group type is assigned to a product group. Follow the IMG menu path SCM
Extended Warehouse Management • SCM Basis • Master Data • Product •
Product Group • Define Product Group. Click New Entries and maintain
the Product Group field, as shown in Figure 5.15.
Figure 5.15 Define Product Group
Master Data Setup
One primary master data setting needed for this process: maintaining the
product group for the product master. Follow the SAP Easy Access menu path
Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse
Management • Master Data • Product Maintain Product or execute Transaction
/SAPAPO/MAT1. Then, under the Properties 2 tab, maintain product group types
and product groups for the product master, as shown in Figure 5.16.
Figure 5.16 Product Master: Maintain Product Group for Product Master
Process Demo
In this section, we’ll go through an inbound goods receipt process using SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling step by step:
1. Create a purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To create a purchase order, execute Transaction ME21N. Input the supplier,
material, purchase order quantity, plant, and receiving storage location,
and any other details required by your business process, and click Save, as
shown in Figure 5.17.
© 

337
Figure 5.17 Create a Purchase Order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
2. Create an inbound delivery in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To create an inbound delivery, execute Transaction VL31N and enter the
Supplier and Purchase Order and other details, as needed, and click
Continue and Save to generate an inbound delivery, as shown in
Figure 5.18.
Figure 5.18 Create Inbound Delivery with Reference to Purchase Order in SAP ERP or
SAP S/4HANA
3. Create a loading appointment with reference to a purchase order in
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
To book the appointment in SAP NetWeaver, execute Transaction NWBC
and select the Dock Appointment Scheduling tab. Then, click Maintain
Appointment - Textual and enter a loading point sand reference
document number and click Save to create the appointment, as shown in
Figure 5.19.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

338
Figure 5.19 Create Appointment: Textual
4. Book a time slot for a loading appointment in SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling
To book a time slot for an appointment in SAP NetWeaver, execute
Transaction NWBC and select the Dock Appointment Scheduling tab.
Then, click Create Appointment - Textual and select a planned arrival at
checkpoint time to maintain the appointment and save, as shown in
Figure 5.20.
Figure 5.20 Maintain Appointment: Textual
5. Process a TU in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
To process a truck at a checkpoint in SAP NetWeaver, execute Transaction
NWBC and select the Dock Appointment Scheduling tab. Then, click
Process Appointments and enter the loading point and appointment
number from the previous step. Next, click Arrival at Checkpoint after
which the Status field will be updated with Arrived at Checkpoint, as
shown in Figure 5.21.
© 

339
Figure 5.21 TU Arrival at Checkpoint
6. Warehouse worker assigns a door to the TU in SAP EWM
To assign a door to a TU, execute Transaction /SCWM/TU and, in the Find
Appointment Number field, enter the appointment number from the
previous step. Click Execute. The TU will be displayed with a door
assigned, as shown in Figure 5.22.
Figure 5.22 TU Door Assignment
7. Assign an inbound delivery to a TU in SAP EWM
To assign a door to a TU, execute Transaction /SCWM/TU, enter the TU
from the previous step, and click Execute. Upon execution, TU will be
displayed. Click Assign del. Immediately and input the inbound delivery.
Then, click Execute, and now the inbound delivery is assigned to TU, as
shown in Figure 5.23, under the Assigned Del. tab.
Figure 5.23 Assignment of Inbound Delivery to TU
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

340
8. Perform goods receipt and putaway process in SAP EWM using RF
(handheld) device
To perform goods receipt and putaway, execute Transaction /SCWM/RFUI
and follow the path e RF- 03 • Inbound Process- 04 • Receiving of
Handling Unit- 01 • Rec. HU by Delivery Option, as shown in Figure 5.24.
Figure 5.24 Perform Goods Receipt and Putaway
9. Truck departs from checkpoint as indicated by appointment clerk in
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
To process a truck at a checkpoint in SAP NetWeaver, execute Transaction
NWBC and select the Dock Appointment Scheduling tab. Then, click
Process Appointments and enter the loading point and appointment
number from earlier steps. Next, click Departure from Checkpoint, and
the status of the appointment will be updated to Departed from
Checkpoint as shown in Figure 5.25.
Figure 5.25 TU Departure from Checkpoint
10. Display the status of a TU in SAP EWM
To display the status of a TU in SAP EWM, execute Transaction /SCWM/TU
and enter the transportation number from the previous step in the TU
field. Next, press (Enter), and under the Status tab, the status should
now be Departure from Checkpoint, as shown in Figure 5.26.
© 

341
Figure 5.26 TU Status
Note
The inbound goods receipt process using SAP EWM and SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is now complete.

sections.title: Dock Appointment Planning in SAP EWM
sections.text:
5.2.2 Dock Appointment Planning in SAP EWM
In this business process, the TU is the processing object of the transport. A TU is
assigned to outbound deliveries and linked to warehouse processing. This
process involves the creation of the TU followed by appointment creation in SAP
EWM. We’ll walk through both inbound and outbound processes in this section.
Inbound Process
Let’s focus first on the inbound goods receipt business process, specifically a
scenario where the TU is created in SAP EWM with yard management along with
dock appointment execution.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 5.27, the business process for inbound deliveries using SAP
Dock Appointment Scheduling with yard management involves the following
steps:
1. The process begins with the creation of an inbound delivery document
(with reference to a purchase order) in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The
inbound delivery is replicated to SAP EWM. A warehouse operator generates
a TU in SAP EWM and associates the inbound delivery with it. These
elements form the planned appointment in SAP EWM as well in SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

342
Figure 5.27 Creation of TU (With Yard Management)
2. The appointment planner then determines the loading point and assigns a
time slot for the provisional appointment. Afterwards, the provisional
appointment is converted into a planned order within SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling.
3. Upon the TU’s arrival at the warehouse, the checkpoint clerk directs the
truck to the assigned checkpoint. A warehouse operator further assigns the
TU to a door.
4. The TU is unloaded and is directed to a checkpoint for release by a
checkpoint clerk.
5. All yard movements, such as the ad-hoc moving of a truck or TU from a
checkpoint to a door or parking area (and vice versa), take place in the
system as yard management movements.

Outbound Process
Let’s look more deeply into the outbound goods issue business process,
specifically a scenario where the TU is created in SAP EWM based on dock
appointment execution.
Business Process
The business process for outbound delivery using SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling with yard management involves the following steps:
1. As shown in Figure 5.50, to initiate the outbound process, a warehouse
operator generates a TU within SAP EWM and associates it with the
outbound delivery. This action automatically creates a provisional
appointment in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling.
Figure 5.50 Dock Appointment Planning in SAP EWM: Outbound Process
2. The appointment planner then determines the loading point and assigns a
time slot for the provisional appointment. Afterwards, the provisional
appointment is converted into a planned order within SAP Dock
Appointment Scheduling.
3. Upon arrival of the truck at the warehouse, the checkpoint clerk directs the
truck to the assigned checkpoint in the system. Once the loading process is
finished, the checkpoint clerk releases the truck from the checkpoint and
authorizes its departure from the warehouse door.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

354
Process Demo
In this section, we’ll go through the outbound goods issue process using SAP
Dock Appointment scheduling step by step:
1. Initiate a customer sales order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA

Order type and Sales area sections. Press (Enter). On the next screen,
enter all the required details for sales order creation, such as material, order

delivery in SAP EWM

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
5.3 Summary
Great! You’re all set to start working on dock appointment scheduling. In this
chapter, we provided an overview of SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling: You
learned how it integrates with other systems and the necessary requirements for
implementing SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. We explored the process of
receiving inbound goods using planning features in SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling. We walked you through the steps involved in scheduling dock
appointments for incoming shipments and the benefits it brings to logistics
processes. You learned about the planning aspect of dock appointments in an
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling system, both for inbound and outbound
processes. We discussed how TUs are planned in SAP EWM. In addition, we
explored various SAP roles and SAP Fiori apps that SAP has released specifically
for the dock appointment scheduling functionality. These tools enable users to
effectively manage and monitor dock appointments. By covering these topics,
you should now have a comprehensive understanding of SAP Dock Appointment
Scheduling, its integration with SAP systems, the inbound goods receipt process,
planning in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling, and other SAP tools available for
managing dock appointments.
© 

361
6 Warehouse Automation Systems
A warehouse automation system encompasses a meticulously coordinated
amalgamation of components that, through synergy, optimize efficiency,
precision, and productivity within the warehouse. Ranging from automated
storage and retrieval systems and robotic picking systems to conveyors,
sortation systems, warehouse management system (WMS) software, and
automated guided vehicles (AGVs), these components spearhead progress
in the industry, empowering businesses to meet the ever-mounting
demands of the contemporary world. This chapter delves into an array of
warehouse automation components that can be seamlessly integrated with
SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM). Moreover, we provide an
extensive exploration of diverse automation system components, including
material flow systems, warehouse robotics systems, automated storage and
retrieval systems, and AGVs.
The integration of SAP EWM with warehouse automation systems aims to create
a seamless and tightly synchronized environment where manual and automated
processes work in harmony. This integration enables businesses to leverage the
benefits of automation technology while maintaining control and visibility over
warehouse operations through a unified system. The integration of SAP EWM
enables seamless data exchange, efficient process coordination, optimized
resource utilization, and enhanced traceability. By leveraging the power of
automation alongside a robust WMS like SAP EWM, organizations can achieve
greater operational excellence and stay competitive in the fast-paced world of
modern warehousing.
This chapter commences by providing an overview of warehouse automation
systems. We discuss detailed information about the different warehouse
automation systems that are being utilized in state-of-the-art warehouses, as
well as their integration with WMSs.

application in both inbound and outbound processes. This chapter covers
